title: Switchboard bootstraps Sentry and OpenTelemetry from one module imported first, and tracing starts only when it is requested and a destination is configured
content:
`src/observability.mts` is imported as the very first thing in `src/index.mts`, because the OpenTelemetry instrumentations (`http`, `express`, `pg`, `graphql`) register require-time hooks at load — **the import order must not change**. What actually runs is decided by environment:

- `SENTRY_DSN` set → Sentry error reporting is initialized.
- `ENABLE_TRACING=true` or `NODE_ENV=production`, **and** at least one trace destination (`TEMPO_ENDPOINT` or `SENTRY_DSN`) → OpenTelemetry tracing starts. Spans go to Tempo over OTLP HTTP if `TEMPO_ENDPOINT` is set, and/or to Sentry via `SentrySpanProcessor` if `SENTRY_DSN` is set. When both are set, **the same trace IDs appear in Tempo and Sentry** and cross-link in Grafana.
- Tracing requested but no destination → a warning, and tracing is **not** started. This avoids patching `http`/`express`/`pg`/`graphql` and generating spans only to drop them.
- `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` set → metrics export to that OTLP HTTP endpoint via a periodic reader (`OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL`, default 60000 ms); reactor metrics from `@powerhousedao/opentelemetry-instrumentation-reactor` flow through the same global meter provider.

If neither Sentry nor a tracing destination is configured the module is a no-op: no exporters, no instrumentations. Supporting variables: `SENTRY_ENV`, `SENTRY_RELEASE` (must match the version CI uploaded source maps for; defaults to `v${npm_package_version}`), `SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE` (0.1), `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` (`switchboard`), `TENANT_ID` (`default`, slices traces per tenant). Tracing is off by default outside production, so a bare `pnpm dev` needs none of this; to exercise the pipeline locally, point `TEMPO_ENDPOINT` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` at a local collector and run with `ENABLE_TRACING=true`.

_Source: apps/switchboard/README.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.74)._
